questions.question:

Which two objects should you create? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.

questions.explanation:

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are a Dynamics 365 Finance developer. You have the following Extended Data Types (EDTs):  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783895726951-vovlb4d3.png)  
  
You plan to modify the EDT properties by using an extension.  
  
You need to determine which operations are possible.  
  
Which operation is possible?

options.text: Create an extension for AccountBase and decrease the field size.
Create a derived EDT for AccountBase and increase the field size.
Create a derived EDT for AccountId and increase the field size.
Create an extension for AccountBase and increase the field size.

questions.explanation:
A string-size change through an EDT extension is permitted only for a root EDT, and the replacement size must be equal to or greater than the existing size. AccountBase is the root EDT, so its size can be increased through an extension; AccountId is derived and cannot have its string size changed this way.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are a Dynamics 365 Finance developer.

Team Foundation Version Control lets pending changes be compared with either the workspace version—the version originally checked out from source control—or the latest version in the team codebase. questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses Dynamics 365 Finance.  
  
You implement the `Insert` method for a table that you create. The class must meet these requirements:  
  
- If `FieldA` equals “Hello,” `FieldB` must save the integer value `10`.  
- If `FieldA` equals “World,” `FieldB` must save the integer value `20`.  
- Otherwise, `FieldB` must save the integer `0`.  
  
You need to implement the code.  
  
Which two code segments can you use? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
An X++ `switch` branch exits when it reaches `break`, so a switch with separate `Hello`, `World`, and `default` branches assigns 10, 20, or 0 as required. An `if`/`else if`/`else` chain is also mutually exclusive and supplies the required default assignment. Without `break`, X++ switch execution falls through to subsequent cases; an unconditional assignment after conditional logic also overwrites the matching result.

**Learn more:** [X++ conditional statements - Finance & Operations | Dynamics 365](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/fin-ops-core/dev-itpro/dev-ref/xpp-conditional)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are training a new Dynamics 365 Finance developer.  
  
You need to recommend where asynchronous integrations should be used rather than synchronous integrations.  
  
For which scenario should you recommend asynchronous integration?

options.text: A retailer requires all new customer data captured at point of sale (POS) terminals through the day sent back to the system.
A retailer wants to ensure gift card balances are communicated back to the system from point of sale (POS) terminals in near real-time.
A manufacturer wants to move production data from an on-premises deployment Dynamics 365 Finance in near real-time.
A warehouse wants to track movement of all inventory from scanners to the system.

questions.explanation:
Asynchronous integration is suited to high-volume data processing when slight delays are acceptable. Sending customer data captured at POS terminals throughout the day can be processed in bulk without requiring an immediate response, unlike gift-card balance and near-real-time operational updates.

**Learn more:** [TechTalk: Integration patterns for finance and operations apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/guidance/techtalks/integrate-finance-operations-overview) · [Data entities overview - Finance & Operations](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/fin-ops-core/dev-itpro/data-entities/data-entities)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are onboarding a new Dynamics 365 Finance developer.  
  
You need to describe the relationships among models, packages, and projects to the new hire.  
  
Which three design concepts should you explain? Each correct answer represents a complete solution.

options.text: A project can contain elements from multiple models.
A model is a group or collection of elements that constitute a distributable software solution.
A Visual Studio project can belong to more than one model.
A model is a design time concept.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses Dynamics 365 finance and operations apps.  
  
A user reports that a custom report is not producing the expected results. After you update the report, you receive an alert about conflicting report changes when you check it in to source control.  
  
You need to troubleshoot the source of the conflict.  
  
What are two causes of the conflict? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: You created an annotation on a prior version of the report in source control.
A developer rolled back the changeset at the same time you were working on the report.
You did not perform a Get Latest Version from source control prior to working on the report.
A developer requested a code review of the prior report changeset which was approved by a reviewer.
A developer modified the report at the same time and created a shelveset of their changes.

questions.explanation:
TFVC requires conflicts to be resolved when a pending workspace change conflicts with the latest server version during check-in. Working without first getting the latest version can leave the report based on an obsolete server version. A concurrent rollback can create and check in a conflicting server-side change to the same report. A shelveset is not checked in, and annotations and code-review approval do not themselves alter the report version in source control.

**Learn more:** [Resolve command (Team Foundation Version Control)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/repos/tfvc/resolve-command?view=azure-devops) · [Get command (Team Foundation Version Control)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/repos/tfvc/get-command?view=azure-devops)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A developer submits code for a quality-assurance review. Several code lines use the `var` data type.

options.text: var var1 = systemDataGet(); var1 = var1 ? today():ג€Not todayג€;

questions.explanation:
In X++, var performs one-time type inference from the initializer and the variable remains strongly typed to that inferred type for its scope. Declaring var var1 = true; infers a boolean type, and because X++ represents boolean values as integers under the hood, integer literals are implicitly assignable to and interchangeable with boolean expressions; this makes the later ternary assignment var1 = true ? 10 : false; type-consistent and able to compile, since both ternary results resolve to boolean-compatible values. Statements that reference a variable within its own declaration before it exists, or combine ternary branches of genuinely incompatible types such as a date literal with a string literal, or an integer literal with a string literal, without an explicit conversion function, fail X++ compile-time type checking.

A company uses Dynamics 365 Finance.  
  
You are conducting a code review of several code segments that use the Boolean data type.  
  
You need to validate the segments for the correct X++ structure.  
  
Which two code statements will compile? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
In X++, an equality comparison can be assigned directly to a `boolean`. Integer values are also interpreted as Boolean values: `1` is true and `0` is false, so a ternary expression whose branches are `1` and `0` can be assigned to a Boolean. The ternary operator requires both result branches to have the same type. A quoted `48` is a string literal, and X++ has no automatic conversion between strings and integers, so comparing `8*6` with `'48'` does not compile.

questions.explanation:
A root EDT can have its string size changed through an extension only to a value equal to or greater than its existing size. You need to configure change tracking for particular fields in the entity.  
  
Which option should you enable?
questions.explanation:
For BYOD change tracking, **Enable custom query** lets a developer supply a query that evaluates changes and is intended for complex requirements that track changes from only a selected set of fields. **Enable primary table** tracks any field change in the primary table, while **Enable entire entity** tracks changes in all tables of the entity.

options.text: select vehicle order by VehicleIdIdx desc;
select vehicle order by VehicleIdIdx asc;

questions.explanation:
In X++ embedded SQL, the `index` keyword orders selected records according to the specified index. Because `VehicleIdIdx` is the index on `VehicleId`, `select vehicle index VehicleIdIdx;` returns the records in that index order, which is ascending. An `order by` clause requires a field identifier, so an index name cannot be used there.

**Learn more:** [Select statement - Finance & Operations | Dynamics 365](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/fin-ops-core/dev-itpro/dev-ref/xpp-data/xpp-select-statement)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company needs a Power Apps app that allows users to view and create new leads in Dynamics 365 from the app.  
  
The data is held in a custom entity named `LeadsTable`, which cannot be accessed outside Dynamics 365.  
  
You need to make the data accessible outside Dynamics 365.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Enable IsPublic for the data entity linked to the LeadsTable.
Assign the create, read, update, and delete operations for the LeadsTable to the sales associate role.
Enable all create, read, update, and delete operations on the LeadsTable table.
Create an aggregate data entity for the LeadsTable.
Enable data management capabilities on the data entity.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is using Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management. You create a customization in a development environment.

**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: In Visual Studio, export the project and upload the project to the asset library.

options.text: Decorate the class with the ExtensionOf attribute.

You need to enable debugging in Visual Studio so that an existing breakpoint is hit while the solution is open.  
  
Which three methods can you use? Each correct answer provides a complete solution. (Choose three.)  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Using Visual Studio to debug, attach the debugger to the devenv.exe process.
Using Visual Studio to debug, start debugging with your start-up object.
Using Visual Studio to debug, attach the debugger to the IIS process.
Using Visual Studio to debug, attach the debugger to the X++ compiler process.

questions.explanation:
Visual Studio can start an X++ debugging session with F5 or by starting the configured start-up object. The Visual Studio IDE process and the X++ compiler process do not host the running application code.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is developing a new solution in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management. Customers will be able to use the solution in their own implementations.  
  
Several classes in the solution are intended to be extended by customers in other implementations to support unique requirements.  
  
Certain methods must appear in the output window during the build process to advise other developers about the methods’ intent.  
  
You need to implement the statements for the methods.  
  
What should you implement?
questions.explanation:
Attributes are the X++ mechanism that can influence the compiler and surface messages in the build output window. Specifically, decorating a class or method with SysObsoleteAttribute causes the X++ compiler to emit a warning (or error) with an explanatory message whenever the item is used, which is exactly how you advise other developers about a method's intent during the build. Comments, global variables, and properties do not produce build-time output messages, and info() only writes to the Infolog at runtime, not during the build. Because the classes are meant to be extended by other developers, attributes such as SysObsoleteAttribute are the correct implementation.

**Learn more:** [X++ attribute classes](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/fin-ops-core/dev-itpro/dev-ref/xpp-attribute-classes) · [Deprecate functionality with SysObsoleteAttribute](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/fin-ops-core/dev-itpro/dev-tools/lock-models)

Does this solution achieve the goal?
questions.explanation: A field’s size is governed by the EDT assigned to that field and its inheritance chain. `BasicCalendarID` derives from `CalendarID`; `CalendarName` is a separate sibling EDT. A derived EDT based on `CalendarName` therefore does not affect a `BasicCalendarID` field or increase its length.

Does this solution satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
String size can be extended only on a root EDT. `CalendarID` is the root EDT for the derived `BasicCalendarID`, so increasing `CalendarID`’s string size through an extension increases the size available to fields that use `BasicCalendarID`, including the `WorkCalendar.BasicCalendarID` column.\

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses Dynamics 365 finance and operations apps.

questions.explanation:

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses Dynamics 365 Finance.  
  
Two processes try to update the same customer record simultaneously. One update fails.  
  
You need to resolve the issue by overriding the table concurrency model.  
  
Which `select` statement should you use?

options.text: select firstonly optimisticLock custTable where custTable.AccountNum == '000001';
select firstonly forupdate custTable where custTable.AccountNum == '000001';
select firstonly pessimisticLock custTable where custTable.AccountNum == '000001';
select firstonly firstFast custTable where custTable.AccountNum == '000001';

questions.explanation:
The X++ `pessimisticLock` keyword overrides the table setting and forces pessimistic concurrency control. It locks the selected customer record so concurrent update attempts are serialized, preventing an optimistic-concurrency update conflict. Microsoft documents `pessimisticLock` as the lock option that forces pessimistic concurrency even when the table uses a different setting.

Does this solution satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
The AFTERHOURS period restricts job starts to the configured after-hours window, and BATCHGROUP2 supplies High priority. A Daily recurrence runs every calendar day, including weekends, rather than only on weekdays; therefore, it does not meet the required weekday-only schedule.\

Does this solution meet the goal?

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are a Dynamics 365 Finance developer.  
  
You need to describe the performance benefits of the different concurrency models.  
  
What are three performance advantages of optimistic concurrency control compared with pessimistic concurrency control? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
> NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Records are locked as soon as they are retrieved from the database.
Records remain available for other processes while they are selected from the database.
Records are locked for a shorter length of time.
Fewer resources are used to lock records during updates.
One record cannot be selected for update by two different processes at the same time.

questions.explanation:
Optimistic concurrency leaves rows unlocked while they are read and detects a conflicting change when an update is attempted. This keeps records available to other processes, shortens lock duration, and reduces server resources required for record locking. Microsoft documents that optimistic concurrency does not lock rows on read and improves performance because record locks require additional server resources.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing a utility to process a large set of transactions in a Dynamics 365 Finance system.  
  
You need to make sure that all exceptions are caught so that a retry mechanism can be implemented.  
  
Which three exception literals can you use? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct answer is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
`UpdateConflict` and `DuplicateKeyException` are optimistic-concurrency transaction exceptions for which X++ supports retry handling. `TransientSqlConnectionError` occurs for transient SQL connection failures, commonly during large transactions or high database load; after the transaction is canceled, the outer transaction or application logic can be retried. `CLRError` and the fatal `Error` literal are not the applicable retry exceptions. questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company that uses Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management needs to be able to import products from Excel files stored in a SharePoint folder.  
  
You need to configure Electronic reporting (ER) so that files can be imported automatically from SharePoint.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Manually upload files to the ER workspace and run the import from there.
Modify the ER model mapping to use a To destination type of file and specify SharePoint as the output location.
Configure a document type that connects to the SharePoint folder and assign it as a file source for the ER format.
Create an ER format and set its data source to SharePoint on the Data sources page.

questions.explanation:
Automated SharePoint-based import through Electronic reporting requires creating a document type (Organization administration > Document management > Document types) whose Location is set to SharePoint and that points to the SharePoint folder containing the files to import. That document type is then selected as the file source on the Electronic reporting source page (Organization administration > Electronic reporting > Electronic reporting source) for the relevant ER format. Once configured, the ER model mapping (of the 'To destination' type) that uses this format can run—manually or as a recurring batch job—to automatically pick up and import files placed in the SharePoint folder, moving them to archive/warning/error folders as appropriate after processing.

**Learn more:** [Configure data import from SharePoint - Finance & Operations | Dynamics 365 | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/fin-ops-core/dev-itpro/analytics/er-configure-data-import-sharepoint) · [Configure document management - Finance & Operations | Dynamics 365 | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/fin-ops-core/dev-itpro/organization-administration/configure-document-management)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company that uses Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management has noticed that various posting operations performed on sales orders cause the user interface to freeze, preventing users from performing other tasks while the operation runs.  
  
The company wants to improve system performance by resolving this issue. You need to implement Real Async feature enhancements to SysOperations for sales orders.  
  
Which two methods should you extend? Each correct answer presents part of the solution. (Choose two.)
questions.explanation:
To implement the Real Async feature enhancements for SysOperations, you extend the SysOperationServiceController class and override two methods. The canRunAsRealAsync method controls whether the operation is allowed to run asynchronously without blocking the client; it returns false by default and must be overridden (often gated by a feature flag) to return true so the operation executes as real async. The getSysRealAsyncOperationId method returns the identifier that ties the async operation status to a specific record, such as the SalesId of the sales order being confirmed, so users can track the status of that operation; it returns an empty string by default and must be overridden to supply this ID.

**Learn more:** [Real async feature enhancements - Finance & Operations](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/fin-ops-core/dev-itpro/dev-tools/real-async)
